title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 412
paragraphs: As for the son, those who went for him found that he was no longer alive but had been cut down first of all; Psammenitos himself, however, they raised from his place and brought into the presence of Cambyses, with whom he continued to live for the rest of his time without suffering any violence. And if he had known how to keep himself from meddling with mischief, he would have received Egypt to rule over, since the Persians are accustomed to honor the sons of kings, and even when kings have revolted from them, they give back the power into the hands of their sons. That this is their established rule, one may judge by many instances besides, and especially by the case of Thannyras son of Inaros, who received back the power his father had held, and by that of Pausiris son of Amyrtaios, who also received back his father's power — though it is certain that no men ever to this time did more harm to the Persians than Inaros and Amyrtaios. As it was, however, Psammenitos devised evil and received the reward that was due: he was found to be inciting the Egyptians to revolt; and when this became known to Cambyses, Psammenitos drank bull's blood and died at once. So he came to his end.
